status: Prospective source-runner acceptance. Publish before the new runner's fault-injection evaluation; no source mutation is yet counted as detected.
purpose: Prove that the optional same-runner CPU checkpoint collector rejects tampered source, invalid sweep data and weakened timing schedules. The user's original DSP, sound, CPU and compatibility tolerances remain unchanged.

fixed_request.checkpoint_source: An immutable full 40-hex commit SHA already in the checkout; the manifest additionally pins its original 40-hex benchmark-source blob
fixed_request.reporter_source: The full 64-hex SHA-256 must match the checked-in unchanged existing reporter
fixed_request.timing_order: Compile every checkpoint before timing; then run round-major: all checkpoints' first rounds, all second rounds, all third rounds; each subprocess completes before the next starts
fixed_request.recorded_host_work: Capture CPU, compiler, process names, clock/frequency and cgroup state only outside each benchmark subprocess

round_acceptance.source: Unchanged original 27-case/51-row source_factory_benchmark, exactly 48 kHz/256 frames/1024 held callbacks, no --quick and no fallback/retry
round_acceptance.metadata: Caller-verified full commit and baseline suite; quick_subset=false, callbacks_per_held_phase=1024; original metadata still disclaims DAW/hardware qualification
round_acceptance.csv: Exactly 51 distinct (rate, block, mode, scenario, initial_selector, phase) rows, each rate=48000 and block=256, finite median/p99/peak/rms, no nonfinite rendered samples
round_acceptance.integrity: Verified source commit/tree, expected benchmark blob, clean source checkout, unmodified executable SHA-256 before each timed subprocess
round_acceptance.serialization: All raw rounds and logs retained; never re-run or discard an unfavourable round; p99 and deadline misses originate from the same round whose median was selected per fixture

source_mutation_observers: Truncate the fixed schedule to two rounds; the exact three-round order check must fail.
Reverse the checkpoint order within one round; the registered order check must fail.
Accept a one-round request or a seven-character source revision; the immutable request gate must fail.
Accept a duplicate checkpoint label or commit; the request gate must fail.
Ignore the reporter SHA-256, source SHA, benchmark blob, source dirtiness or executable SHA-256; each respective tampered input must fail.
Ignore source_commit_caller_verified, suite or quick_subset metadata; each invalid control must fail.
Ignore completed=false, 26 cases or 50 declared result rows; each malformed completion record must fail.
Accept 50 CSV rows, duplicate fixture rows, 44.1 kHz / 128-frame rows, a nonfinite metric or a nonfinite rendered-sample count; each malformed CSV must fail.
mutation_method: Mutate the actual Python source in a temporary copy, import/compile it successfully, and call the affected observer with a real sealed CSV/metadata fixture plus one deliberate bad value. A mutant is killed only if the original positive control passes and the mutant normally accepts an input its intended invariant rejects; crashes, syntax failures, timeouts and unrelated exceptions are not kills. Restore and re-evaluate the unmodified source afterward.
not_claimed: This is a collection/provenance gate. Passing it does not meet either CPU target, validate an analog circuit law, prove absence of hypervisor interference, or replace the mandatory audio/accuracy and strict compatibility gates.
